title: Self-citation with no changes fixed in advance: write the whole book, score a sample of its pages, and separate the section from the page
statement: Work on K-003-open-1, public practice split only; nothing here is scored on hidden pages. Question: does a meaningless procedure need changes fixed in advance at page and section boundaries, or does reuse of recent words make pages and sections differ by itself? Procedure: the generator behind R-012 to R-017 with its drift switched off, so one glyph table fitted on all public training pages and nothing fitted by position; its only memory is reuse (a quarter of words are one of the last 15 words with one glyph changed, a quarter are a word standing at least twice among the last 300 words, written again whole). Two ways of handing the text to the scorer. (A) Contiguous, as every attack so far: 2,000 lines laid in order onto the 34 evaluation pages. Result: all 16 established facts and the pending first-line fact hold on 2 of 2 seeds, including F-011 (near-minus-far page similarity 0.111 against the manuscript's 0.074) and F-018 (0.96 bits against 1.18). (B) Whole book, sampled: the same writer writes about 12,000 to 15,000 lines without a break, the book is cut into pages of 24 lines (the public mean), and each page is kept with probability 0.15, the share of pages the scorer sees; only the kept pages are sent. Result on three seeds: F-011 fails on two (0.026, -0.012, 0.036; manuscript 0.074), everything else holds, including F-009 and F-016 (0.25 to 0.26 against 0.31) and F-018 (0.95 to 0.98 against 1.18). Three things follow. First, an artefact of the attack format: the scorer lays an attacker's text end to end onto a sample of pages, so two sampled pages that stand 15 pages apart in the manuscript receive text written a page or two apart, and a memory of 300 words reaches across them. Under (A), F-011 is passed by a procedure with no long-range structure at all. R-012 did not rely on this (its table drifts over a planned book the size of the sample, which amounts to (B) for a drifting table), but the format allows it and later attacks on long-range facts should be sent in form (B) and say so. Second, on K-003-open-1 itself: reuse alone, with no change fixed in advance, gives pages their own vocabulary but does not make neighbouring pages more alike than distant ones once the book is sampled honestly; some slow change of the table along the book is needed for that (R-012 used a table refitted on a sliding window of 20 public pages). Whether that change must sit at the section and Currier boundaries is still not measured on hidden pages: step P-G-002 found on public pages that the manuscript's lowest adjacent-page scores fall on those transitions and that only tables switched at the boundaries reproduce it, and the measurement language still lacks that statistic. Third, F-018 is not a long-range fact as registered: procedure (B), which has no section structure and fails F-011, passes it on 3 of 3 seeds, because its null deals words across all pages and so is beaten by page-level reuse alone (the fact's own source warned of this). Proposed: (1) a reviewed code change adding a null that keeps every page whole and deals whole pages among the sections (or rotates the section labels along the page order), then F-018 re-registered against it; (2) the transition statistic of P-G-002; (3) a line in the red-team guide that attacks on facts about distance between pages state how the text was sampled. Limits: three seeds, one page length, one sampling rate; the kept pages are cut every 24 lines while the scorer cuts at the real page lengths; F-011 passing on one seed of three shows the fact has little margin on a sample of 34 pages.
check: Reproduce (A) and (B) from the stated procedure on the practice split; then, once a page-keeping null exists, fact.json for the section fact against it, and attack.json in form (B) from both the drifting and the drift-free procedure.
